newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand dollar ends lower after light session.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand dollar ends lower after light session.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ducked below US$0.6900 on Monday to end the session on a weaker note after a light day's trade.
The Kiwi closed at US$0.6893/00, down from 0.6910/20 this morning, having traded a tight range over the weekend.
Dealers said the Kiwi had opened a little firmer, possibly on comments from Treasurer Winston Peters in the Philippines overnight.

Peters, in an interview with Reuters Financial Television, said he expected the New Zealand dollar to rise further in the long term. Peters was in Cebu for a meeting of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) finance ministers.
The stronger opening was followed by selling by a local bank and from Asia, down to a low of 0.6895.
A bounce followed with some exporter buying, which took it back up to US$0.6912. "Now it seems to be a bit of a sinking lid. It's just drifting off a bit," said one Auckland dealer.
Overnight, Asia was likely to buy again, but the currency was not expected to venture far outside a 0.6895-10 range.
